question_text: A 25-year-old woman presents to the emergency department with sudden onset of lower limb weakness for the past 2 days. She says she also hasn’t been able to urinate for that same period. There is no history of trauma, fever, weight loss, recent respiratory tract infection, or diarrhea. She has a past medical history of left arm weakness 18 months ago that resolved spontaneously. Her father had type 2 diabetes mellitus, ischemic heart disease, and left-sided residual weakness secondary to an ischemic stroke involving the right middle cerebral artery. Her vital signs include: blood pressure 120/89 mm Hg, temperature 36.7°C (98.0°F), pulse 78/min, and respiration rate 16/min. Muscle strength is 3/5 in both lower limbs with increased tone and exaggerated deep tendon reflexes. The sensation is decreased up to the level of the umbilicus. Muscle strength, tone, and deep tendon reflexes in the upper limbs are normal. On flexion of the neck, the patient experiences electric shock-like sensations that travel down to the spine. Funduscopic examination reveals mildly swollen optic discs bilaterally. Which of the following is the next best step in management for this patient?
